ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(eval): report success counts and 95% Wilson intervals at every aggregation level (#4628)

* feat(eval): report success counts and 95% Wilson intervals at every aggregation level

A success rate over 10 to 50 episodes is a binomial estimate with a wide
interval (9/10 is compatible with roughly 60% to 98%), and lerobot-eval
reported it as a bare number. Every success rate in eval_info.json now
carries n_success, n_episodes and pc_success_ci95 (percent), at task, suite
and overall level, and lerobot-eval logs the overall interval.

lerobot.utils.eval_stats adds wilson_interval, success_summary and a
two-sided fisher_exact, standard library only. Reference values in the tests
were checked against scipy.

Existing keys and values are unchanged. Roadmap EVAL-01 (#3832).

* docs: run the eval_stats docstring examples in CI (first entry in the doctest allowlist)

* fix(eval): drop the unused confidence argument from success_summary

Addresses review finding 1. success_summary took a confidence argument but
always wrote the result under pc_success_ci95, so success_summary(flags,
confidence=0.9) returned a 90% interval under a key that says 95. Nothing
passed it, so the argument is gone and the coverage is fixed at 95%, which
makes the key name always true. wilson_interval keeps the argument for callers
that want a different level.

Also rewords the test comment (finding 5): eval_policy yields Python bools
today, and the test accepts 0/1 ints so a future change to the reduction cannot
silently change what gets counted. The old wording sent readers looking for a
backend that does not exist.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(robots): honour the configured sdk_url on EarthRover Mini Plus (#…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(robots): honour the configured sdk_url on EarthRover Mini Plus (#4515)

EarthRoverMiniPlusConfig.sdk_url is the only field that says which Frodobots
SDK server this robot talks to, and __init__ assigned a hardcoded
"http://localhost:8000" instead of reading it. The field had no other reader,
so every configured URL was discarded.

All six HTTP call sites build their URL from self.sdk_base_url, so a caller who
points the robot at a remote SDK is served by whatever answers on the default
port instead. With something listening there, connect() reports success and
POST /control delivers a drive command to a different rover; with nothing
listening, the refusal names http://localhost:8000 rather than the host the
caller configured.

Read config.sdk_url, whose default is the same "http://localhost:8000", so the
local workflow in the setup guide is unchanged.

Adds tests/robots/test_earthrover_mini_plus.py: the configured URL is adopted,
the default is unchanged, every endpoint the robot drives is built from the
configured base, and an unreachable SDK is named by its configured URL.

(cherry picked from commit a473c37ec165e6c443893b00e1f70b74821ceaad)

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(pi05): match time_mlp modules in default PEFT targets (#4494)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(pi05): match time_mlp modules in default PEFT targets (#4494)

PI05Pytorch names the action-expert time projections `time_mlp_in` and
`time_mlp_out`, but `_get_default_peft_targets` inherited the pi0-style
`action_time_mlp_*` names, so the LoRA adapter never targeted these
projections during pi0.5 fine-tuning.

Fix the regex and add a regression test.
